subject: health
title: Launch and diagnostic: respect and boundaries
essentialQuestion: How can understanding relationships, consent, and communication help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Respect includes honoring stated limits, privacy, identity, and equal dignity; a boundary is valid even when another person does not understand or prefer it.
A safe communication plan states the limit clearly, recognizes pressure or danger, identifies an exit, and brings in adult or professional support when direct engagement is unsafe.
For respect and boundaries, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Practice communication and bystander scripts with opt-out from role-play and no personal disclosure.
studentTask: Annotate a supplied fictional exchange about respect and boundaries: underline the stated limit, circle any pressure or respectful check-in, and write a two-sentence response that states a boundary plus a safe next step. Add when a trusted adult should enter the plan.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in respect and boundaries; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the respect and boundaries task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
